evidence_packet.evidence_text: Heaton Park synagogue attack memorial service attended by 800 - BBC News Image source, Family handouts Image caption, Adrian Daulby and Melvin Cravitz, were killed in the attack on the Heaton Park Synagogue in Manchester By Judith Moritz , Special correspondent , Daniel Wittenberg , Senior producer and Angela Ferguson , North West Published 31 August 2026 The Chief Rabbi Ephraim Mirvis and Communities Secretary Angela Rayner were among about 800 people who attended a memorial event for the victims and survivors of last year's Heaton Park synagogue attack. Melvin Cravitz and Adrian Daulby were killed, and three others injured, as they tried to defend their place of worship from attacker Jihad al-Shamie on 2 October 2025. Relatives of the bereaved and some of the survivors were among the speakers at Monday's service of remembrance at the synagogue in Manchester. Prior to the event, Rabbi Daniel Walker said the Jewish community feels less safe now than it did immediately after the attack. He said rising antisemitism, combined with a lack of action to "deal with core problems", had left many members of Heaton Park Hebrew Congregation – and British Jews more widely – feeling increasingly vulnerable. Two seats remained empty for the service, bearing the names of Melvin Cravitz and Adrian Daulby. title: Eccles: Homes will be 'completely dwarfed' by warehouses

evidence_packet.title: Eccles: Homes will be 'completely dwarfed' by warehouses
evidence_packet.lead: Residents have expressed concerns about a lack of proper consultation over the development
evidence_packet.summary: Residents have expressed concerns about a lack of proper consultation over the development
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Eccles: Homes will be 'completely dwarfed' by warehouses - BBC News Image source, BBC/Phil Cunliffe Image caption, Andy Spratt said residents were concerned about the scale of the development and also about what might lie beneath the ground of the former chemical plant site By Phil Cunliffe , Reporting from in Eccles and Angela Ferguson , North West Published 2 hours ago A residents' group has expressed concern that their homes will be "completely dwarfed" by a large warehouse development being built on their doorsteps. The largest warehouse planned for the site in Eccles, Salford, is set to be 60ft (18m) high, according to nearby resident Andy Spratt. He also raised concerns about what could be in the ground at the former site of a chemical plant. A spokesperson for developer Aviva Investors said: "There is no evidence of any contamination from the previous use of the site, nor has any evidence of the presence of chemicals appeared throughout the conveyancing and survey process prior to work starting, nor since work has commenced." Plans for the brownfield site on Lankro Way, close to the Manchester Ship Canal, were granted planning permission by Salford Council in 2022. Consent was later given for Aviva Investors to build seven large storage units. Spratt and fellow resident Holly Muldoon have set up the Stop the Eccles Warehouse campaign group. Spratt told BBC North West Tonight that the end of his street and Boardman Street was "just going to be completely dwarfed by the warehouse" and could lose a lot of morning light as a result. He said it was going to be a 24/7 logistics operation "which means articulated lorries all day, all night, forklift trucks". The Mayor of Greater Manchester Bev Craig has previously said planning rules should be reviewed after complaints

evidence_packet.summary: From early wake-up calls to amazing views, what is work really like when your office is above the clouds?
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Pete Smith always secures the best seat on the plane "No matter the time of year, we always get some sunshine when we go to work," said Capt Smith, who has worked in the aviation industry for 30 years after deciding to pursue his dreams following a decade working for British Gas "It's a fantastic office, there's worse places to work." Bank holiday weekends can be even busier for pilots and cabin crews, with Smith's alarm clock going off at 03:30 BST for a flight to Croatia "I think 06:05 was our departure time," he said. "We tend to go out and back on short haul and then the long haul you literally stay in the hotel overnight "The next lunchtime, wherever you are, you fly back. So it's a busy schedule, the height of summer, a really busy period."

Rabbi Daniel Walker said rising antisemitism, combined with a lack of action to "deal with core problems", had left many members of Heaton Park Hebrew Congregation in Manchester – and British Jews more widely – feeling increasingly vulnerable as the anniversary of the attack approaches. "I think we're actually almost in a harder position than we were even immediately after the attack," he said ahead of a memorial service for the victims and survivors which will take place later today. "I think the sense of vulnerability has grown. It hasn't diminished." Image caption, Yoni Finlay said Jewish people are "having to hide their identity" One of those injured in the attack said his son has since faced death threats and that overall "things don't feel safer". Yoni Finlay was hit by a stray police bullet while helping to barricade the doors as Jihad Al-Shamie attacked the synagogue. Ahead of a memorial service planned for Monday evening, he told BBC Radio 4's Today programme the past year had not been easy but he had been supported by friends and family. title: Driver wrecks Ferrari supercar in M602 crash in Salford

evidence_packet.title: Driver wrecks Ferrari supercar in M602 crash in Salford
evidence_packet.lead: The Ferrari 296 supercar was left a mangled wreck when its driver lost control in the wet, police say
evidence_packet.summary: The Ferrari 296 supercar was left a mangled wreck when its driver lost control in the wet, police say
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A Ferrari supercar has been left a mangled wreck after its driver lost control in wet conditions The red Ferrari 296, which are generally sold brand new for a starting price of between £240,000 and £260,000 before optional extras, was crushed in the crash on the M602 in Salford on Sunday Greater Manchester Police said "luckily" the driver had escaped injury The bonnet of the high performance car was crushed into a pile of mangled metal, with one of the front wheels twisted out of shape, while the other had completely snapped away Police said that "unfortunately there's one less Ferrari 296 in the world" after "the driver of this one lost control in the wet" The force added: "No injuries luckily but please drive to the conditions for everyone's sake."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Anger as workmen rip out 'lovely' Levenshulme alley garden - BBC News Image source, Tom Marrett Image caption, About four households led the project, with other neighbours helping occasionally. By Haider Saleem Reporting from North West Published 31 August 2026 Residents who spent years developing a community garden in an alleyway came home to find workmen had ripped it out. They said they had spent five years growing fruit trees and decking out the Levenshume, Greater Manchester alley - some of it paid for by Manchester City Council funding. But Tom Marrett and Maeve Cowan returned home to find everything gone, including a mature grapevine. Basat Sheikh, the council's executive member for neighbourhoods, and Zahid Hussain said senior officers had been asked to investigate, adding the clearance "should never have happened". The garden runs behind homes between Stanhope Street, Gordon Avenue and Delamere Road. Marrett, 37, a designer who runs a community workshop in Stockport, discovered the clearance while taking out his bins on Friday evening. Image source, Tom Marrett Image caption, Residents transformed the previously fly-tipped alleyway into a community garden with fruit trees, flowers and picnic tables "Normally you're sort of surrounded by all this greenery," he said. "I went out there and I could just see a brick wall. I thought I was dreaming." He described what had happened as a "catastrophe" and said it felt like "cultural vandalism" because the garden was a communal space where neighbours gathered. Image source, Tom Marrett Image caption, Some raised planters survived, but residents said fruit trees, flowers and a mature grapevine were cut down Marrett and Cowan moved to the area about six years ago and began improving the alleyway the following year. evidence_packet.evidence_text: A Ferrari supercar has been left a mangled wreck after its driver lost control in wet conditions The red Ferrari 296, which are generally sold brand new for a starting price of between £240,000 and £260,000 before optional extras, was crushed in the crash on the M602 in Salford on Sunday Greater Manchester Police said "luckily" the driver had escaped injury The bonnet of the high performance car was crushed into a pile of mangled metal, with one of the front wheels twisted out of shape, while the other had completely snapped away Police said that "unfortunately there's one less Ferrari 296 in the world" after "the driver of this one lost control in the wet" The force added: "No injuries luckily but please drive to the conditions for everyone's sake."

The move means thousands of kids now won't have to move schools due to expensive and difficult bus travel Greater Manchester mayor Bev Craig said the free Bee Network bus travel will make life 'that little bit easier' for homeless children during already difficult times The major policy comes into effect following a six-month long Manchester Evening News campaign, which was launched last summer Under government transport rules, youngsters were only eligible for free travel if they lived more than two miles from class (three miles for over-eights) and if no 'suitable school' is nearer. But the smiley little boy from Rochdale had his life cruelly cut short, aged just two, in December 2020 Prolonged exposure to mould at the social flat where his family lived led to the toddler’s death . title: For thousands of homeless children across Greater Manchester, life just got that little bit easier

evidence_packet.title: For thousands of homeless children across Greater Manchester, life just got that little bit easier
evidence_packet.lead: Buses For thousands of homeless children across Greater Manchester, life just got that little bit easier Following a six-month Manchester Evening News campaign, kids in temporary accommodation across the region will be able to travel to and from schoo News Ashlie Blakey Live and
evidence_packet.summary: Buses For thousands of homeless children across Greater Manchester, life just got that little bit easier Following a six-month Manchester Evening News campaign, kids in temporary accommodation across the region will be able to travel to and from schoo News Ashlie Blakey Live and
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Buses For thousands of homeless children across Greater Manchester, life just got that little bit easier Following a six-month Manchester Evening News campaign, kids in temporary accommodation across the region will be able to travel to and from schoo News Ashlie Blakey Live and breaking news reporter 00:01, 01 Sep 2026 Thousands of homeless children in temporary accommodation across Greater Manchester will now be able to travel on buses to and from school for free in a major victory following a Manchester Evening News campaig The measure comes into place today (Tuesday, September 1) and will benefit scores of more than 8,000 children living in temporary housing across the region. The move means thousands of kids now won't have to move schools due to expensive and difficult bus travel Greater Manchester mayor Bev Craig said the free Bee Network bus travel will make life 'that little bit easier' for homeless children during already difficult times The major policy comes into effect following a six-month long Manchester Evening News campaign, which was launched last summer Under government transport rules, youngsters were only eligible for free travel if they lived more than two miles from class (three miles for over-eights) and if no 'suitable school' is nearer. But in Manchester, it is almost impossible to be further than two miles from a school

But the smiley little boy from Rochdale had his life cruelly cut short, aged just two, in December 2020 Prolonged exposure to mould at the social flat where his family lived led to the toddler’s death . His family had pleaded for help to fix the stubborn mould problem that refused to go away, but they did not get the support they needed Following the tragedy, the Manchester Evening News uncovered widespread issues of damp, mould and disrepair on the same estate. Hours later, John Mulcahy was clambering onto the roof of their home in a desperate attempt to save his wife's life As their children watched from a neighbour's house, Mr Mulcahy scaled a drainpipe, ripped off roof tiles and smashed the glass of a skylight. Sadly, it was too late. A raging fire had taken hold Attempts to save Mrs Mulcahy proved impossible. She was later found dead inside by firefighters. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Heywood Bosses issue update after Andy Burnham promise on Heywood getting Metrolink Last year Andy Burnham said spades will be in the ground on the project in Heywood by 2028 Comments News George Lythgoe Local Democracy Reporter 07:51, 31 Aug 2026 Vie Metrolink trams to Heywood have been promised by Andy Burnham. Last year, the former Greater Manchester mayor even said spades could be in the ground by 2028 Now Mr Burnham sits in Downing Street as Prime Minister, his successor in the city-region, Bev Craig, hasn’t mentioned the project. She did speak about the expansion of the tram network to Stockport in her manifesto, but Heywood was omitted Despite this, Transport for Greater Manchester (TfGM) has confirmed they are working on a business case for the Heywood project. It falls under what TfGM calls the Oldham-Rochdale-Heywood-Bury Tram-Train pathfinder The new Metrolink line would connect Bury to Rochdale via Heywood and then loop back through Shaw towards Oldham . However, no plans have been formally approved When opened, the scheme would give Greater Manchester two Metrolink firsts: The first ‘orbital’ Metrolink route, i.e. one which does not go via the city centre, and the first ‘tram-train’, set to be rolled out across the city in coming years

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester canal lost for 91 years after gigantic breach is set to resurface within months A new cafe and canoe and kayak school will be features of the restored length of waterway Comments News Chris Gee Local democracy reporter 07:11, 31 Aug 2026 Vi A section of canal lost since it collapsed 90 years ago is set to be ‘in water’ and enjoyed by the public within months. Part of the Manchester, Bolton and Bury canal near Little Lever was breached in July 1936 Millions of gallons of water from the channel came cascading down into the River Irwell below. The gigantic breach happened close to the Nob End locks, on the canal’s arm towards Bury, with the affected section never restored But work done by Watson Homes, who are building a new 255 home estate alongside the affected waterway at the former Creams Mill site in Little Lever, is set to change that Watson has been restoring a 800 metre section of the waterway as part of the planning permission. The extensive work means the section of canal is set to be ‘in water’ by May 2027 The new section of waterway will also create a destination for visitors as a new café is planned alongside a canoe and kayaking school

It will be the first chance for MPs across the House to probe him on the slew of policies he announced over the summer He is expected to use his Commons debut as Prime Minister, and his first appearance at the despatch box in 16 years, to argue that stronger public control over many of the country’s services can be an engine for economic growth. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Buses For thousands of homeless children across Greater Manchester, life just got that little bit easier Following a six-month Manchester Evening News campaign, kids in temporary accommodation across the region will be able to travel to and from schoo News Ashlie Blakey Live and breaking news reporter 00:01, 01 Sep 2026 Thousands of homeless children in temporary accommodation across Greater Manchester will now be able to travel on buses to and from school for free in a major victory following a Manchester Evening News campaig The measure comes into place today (Tuesday, September 1) and will benefit scores of more than 8,000 children living in temporary housing across the region. The move means thousands of kids now won't have to move schools due to expensive and difficult bus travel Greater Manchester mayor Bev Craig said the free Bee Network bus travel will make life 'that little bit easier' for homeless children during already difficult times The major policy comes into effect following a six-month long Manchester Evening News campaign, which was launched last summer Under government transport rules, youngsters were only eligible for free travel if they lived more than two miles from class (three miles for over-eights) and if no 'suitable school' is nearer. But in Manchester, it is almost impossible to be further than two miles from a school

And in a matter of weeks, it will get bigger and better Awaab Ishak should have been preparing to start his Year Three class at primary school this week. But the smiley little boy from Rochdale had his life cruelly cut short, aged just two, in December 2020 Prolonged exposure to mould at the social flat where his family lived led to the toddler’s death . His family had pleaded for help to fix the stubborn mould problem that refused to go away, but they did not get the support they needed Following the tragedy, the Manchester Evening News uncovered widespread issues of damp, mould and disrepair on the same estate. The scandal sparked Rochdale Boroughwide Housing into action - but other tenants faced the same issues up and down the country Awaab’s Law, named in the toddler’s honour, came into action in England on October 27 last year. Hours later, John Mulcahy was clambering onto the roof of their home in a desperate attempt to save his wife's life As their children watched from a neighbour's house, Mr Mulcahy scaled a drainpipe, ripped off roof tiles and smashed the glass of a skylight. Sadly, it was too late. A raging fire had taken hold Attempts to save Mrs Mulcahy proved impossible. She was later found dead inside by firefighters. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester synagogue attack Dad shot in Manchester synagogue attack says son has faced death threats and 'things don't feel safer' 'Jewish people are having to hide their identity' since the attack last year, Yoni Finlay said Comments News Press Assoc One of the men who was injured during an attack on Heaton Park Synagogue has said his son has since faced death threats and that “things don’t feel safer”, almost a year on from the attack 35-year-old Jihad al-Shamie drove his vehicle into pedestrians and began stabbing attendees outside the Synagogue on Middleton Road on the morning of October 2 last year, on Yom Kippur, the holiest day in the Jewish calendar Within minutes a huge emergency response was on the scene and worshipper Yoni Finlay was hit by a police bullet as he helped to barricade the doors as Jihad Al-Shamie attempted to access the site Along with three others, Mr Finlay was seriously injured in the attack. Melvin Cravitz, 66, died from multiple knife wounds inflicted by Al-Shamie, while Adrian Daulby, 53, was struck by a single gunshot wound to the chest fired by an armed police officer as he held the door shut A pre-inquest review hearing earlier this year heard that Mr Finlay was seriously injured by the same bullet that passed through the door and took Mr Daulby’s life

The school holidays may be drawing to a close this week, but September getaways are extremely popular among those without kids or school-age This summer was predicted to be the busiest on record for the airport. Although figures are yet to be released for August, July was the second-busiest travel month experienced by the airport, with more than 3.3million passengers using the northern travel hub At the start of the summer the airport predicted that more than 5.7million passengers would fly in and out of the airport between Friday, July 17 and the end of the holidays on September 1. evidence_packet.lead: Heywood Bosses issue update after Andy Burnham promise on Heywood getting Metrolink Last year Andy Burnham said spades will be in the ground on the project in Heywood by 2028 Comments News George Lythgoe Local Democracy Reporter 07:51, 31 Aug 2026 Vie Metrolink trams to Heywood h
evidence_packet.summary: Heywood Bosses issue update after Andy Burnham promise on Heywood getting Metrolink Last year Andy Burnham said spades will be in the ground on the project in Heywood by 2028 Comments News George Lythgoe Local Democracy Reporter 07:51, 31 Aug 2026 Vie Metrolink trams to Heywood h
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Heywood Bosses issue update after Andy Burnham promise on Heywood getting Metrolink Last year Andy Burnham said spades will be in the ground on the project in Heywood by 2028 Comments News George Lythgoe Local Democracy Reporter 07:51, 31 Aug 2026 Vie Metrolink trams to Heywood have been promised by Andy Burnham. Last year, the former Greater Manchester mayor even said spades could be in the ground by 2028 Now Mr Burnham sits in Downing Street as Prime Minister, his successor in the city-region, Bev Craig, hasn’t mentioned the project. She did speak about the expansion of the tram network to Stockport in her manifesto, but Heywood was omitted Despite this, Transport for Greater Manchester (TfGM) has confirmed they are working on a business case for the Heywood project. It falls under what TfGM calls the Oldham-Rochdale-Heywood-Bury Tram-Train pathfinder The new Metrolink line would connect Bury to Rochdale via Heywood and then loop back through Shaw towards Oldham . However, no plans have been formally approved When opened, the scheme would give Greater Manchester two Metrolink firsts: The first ‘orbital’ Metrolink route, i.e. one which does not go via the city centre, and the first ‘tram-train’, set to be rolled out across the city in coming years

title: Manchester canal lost for 91 years after gigantic breach is set to resurface within months

evidence_packet.title: Manchester canal lost for 91 years after gigantic breach is set to resurface within months
evidence_packet.lead: Manchester canal lost for 91 years after gigantic breach is set to resurface within months A new cafe and canoe and kayak school will be features of the restored length of waterway Comments News Chris Gee Local democracy reporter 07:11, 31 Aug 2026 Vi A section of canal lost sinc
evidence_packet.summary: Manchester canal lost for 91 years after gigantic breach is set to resurface within months A new cafe and canoe and kayak school will be features of the restored length of waterway Comments News Chris Gee Local democracy reporter 07:11, 31 Aug 2026 Vi A section of canal lost sinc
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester canal lost for 91 years after gigantic breach is set to resurface within months A new cafe and canoe and kayak school will be features of the restored length of waterway Comments News Chris Gee Local democracy reporter 07:11, 31 Aug 2026 Vi A section of canal lost since it collapsed 90 years ago is set to be ‘in water’ and enjoyed by the public within months. Part of the Manchester, Bolton and Bury canal near Little Lever was breached in July 1936 Millions of gallons of water from the channel came cascading down into the River Irwell below. The gigantic breach happened close to the Nob End locks, on the canal’s arm towards Bury, with the affected section never restored But work done by Watson Homes, who are building a new 255 home estate alongside the affected waterway at the former Creams Mill site in Little Lever, is set to change that Watson has been restoring a 800 metre section of the waterway as part of the planning permission. The extensive work means the section of canal is set to be ‘in water’ by May 2027 The new section of waterway will also create a destination for visitors as a new café is planned alongside a canoe and kayaking school

On the return journey to RAF Warrington on Sunday, the team will fly directly over Greater Manchester, with a special flypast over the hospital The route saw the team fly over Lymm, onto Altrincham and then directly over the city centre, before heading out into Tameside and Oldham . From there, the team flew back to their base at RAF Waddington, in Lincolnshire Earlier this week, Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust announced that the Red Arrows would be doing the flypast to 'support them and create a memorable moment' for the children receiving care at the Children's Hospital In a post, Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust said: "We're excited to share that this bank holiday weekend we're in for a real treat - and we want you to enjoy it with us "The world-famous RAF Red Arrows will be carrying out a flypast over Royal Manchester Children's Hospital this Sunday at around 5.15pm - subject to weather and other operational factors on the day

News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Reporter 17 People living near the A555 fear a plan to stop the road flooding could be a 'recipe for disaster' Less than 10 years old, the A555 has faced ‘longstanding challenges’, causing major disruption for drivers. The road links Stockport and Manchester Airport to the wider network but after it opened in 2018, it has been repeatedly affected by flooding Work was done to try and solve the problem but the road has still continued to flood. Credit: ITV News Reform UK and Labour have gone through to the second round of voting in the Greater Manchester Mayoral by-ele Neither Labour's Bev Craig or Reform UK's Sian Astley managed to secure a majority, meaning voters second choice ballots will now be counted to decide an overall winner Five candidates have now been eliminated from the contest to become Greater Manchester mayor – Geraldine Coggins (Green), Phil Eckersley (Conservative), Marcus Farmer (Independent), Richard Kilpatrick (Liberal Democrats) and Marlon West (Restore Britain) The by-election is using a voting system called supplementary vote (SV), which sees voters mark their ballot papers with a first and second choice, and if any candidate wins more than 50% of the first-choice votes, they are declared the winner That has not happened in Greater Manchester, so the top two candidates, Labour’s Bev Craig and Reform UK candidate Sian Astley, move to a second round ITV Granada Reports' Political Correspondent Lise McNally sent the latest from the Co-op Live as counting for the second round got underway

evidence_packet.evidence_text: The family are Altrincham FC season ticket holders Share on WhatsApp Share via Email Lois (second right) with husband Ollie and kids Imogen and Jacob A local mum of two is fighting for her life in hospital after a liver transplant that almost killed her Lois Kinder, 44, was rushed to hospital in mid-July after becoming critically ill with acute liver failure. Within days she was placed in an induced coma and transferred to the specialist liver intensive care unit at Queen Elizabeth Hospital Birmingham, one of only a handful of c On 22 July a donor liver became available, but during the operation she suffered three cardiac arrests after a blood clot blocked the main artery to her lungs, leaving her starved of oxygen for a prolonged period. Surgeons told her husband Ollie more than once that she was unlike Against the odds she pulled through. Six weeks on she is conscious and recognises her family, but the lack of oxygen caused significant brain damage to both sides of her brain. She cannot move, remains on a ventilator and dialysis, and is still in critical care “She’s conscious. She is recognising who we are,” Ollie said. “She’s saying the odd word, albeit very, very weak. She can’t move or anything like that at the moment. They’re hopeful of a form of recovery, but whether she will walk again remains unknown.”

evidence_packet.evidence_text: on WhatsApp Share via Email A blue plaque has been unveiled at a Bowdon house to mark the life of William Wood, the social reformer known as “The Climbing Boys’ Friend” The plaque is at Willow Cottage, 28 Stamford Road, where Wood lived after retiring there in 1847. It was unveiled last week at a ceremony organised by Trafford Council’s Local Studies team, attended by residents, historians, council members, Connor Rand MP and the Friends of Bowd Wood, born in 1782, was a wool merchant who began campaigning in 1826 after seeing a young boy fall to his death inside a chimney onto a live fire. “Climbing boys” were children sent up chimneys to sweep them, often suffering burns, respiratory illness, deformity and suffocation From Bowdon he funded prosecutions against master sweeps who broke child labour laws, put up placards at railway stations and wrote to newspapers He also challenged magistrates and even Queen Victoria over the use of a child sweep at Windsor Castle His work with Lord Shaftesbury included testimony to the House of Lords in 1853, which helped lead to the Chimney Sweepers Act of 1875. Wood died in 1868, aged 85, seven years before the practice was banned. Six chimney sweeps from five towns carried his coffin to St Mary’s Churc

evidence_packet.summary: Oldham Council has secured a court order requiring the removal of an unauthorised encampment from Oldham Edge
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Oldham Council has secured a court order requiring the removal of an unauthorised encampment from Oldham Edge Council officers first visited the site on Thursday 6th August following concerns from residents and people using the park. Officers spoke to those at the encampment, who said they intended to leave by Saturday 8th August As the site had not been vacated, the Council returned with support from Greater Manchester Police on Tuesday 11th August. A formal direction was served under Section 77 of the Criminal Justice and Public Order Act 1994, requiring those at the encampment to leave and remove their The Council also provided information about authorised sites in Greater Manchester, along with advice about health, wellbeing and reporting hate crime After the direction was not followed, the Council began court proceedings. On Monday 17th August, Tameside Magistrates’ Court granted an order requiring the removal of the encampment The site was vacated later that day. A significant amount of waste was left behind, which has now been removed by the Council’s cleansing team

evidence_packet.evidence_text: The Council's Community Safety Service received a Closure Order for a house following reports of persistent anti-social behaviour and criminal activity The order, which is in place for three months, was granted by magistrates under the Anti-Social Behaviour, Crime and Policing Act 2014. The order makes it an offence for anyone, including the occupants, from entering the property while it is in force and restricts access only to Reports linked to the address included disorderly and intimidating behaviour, suspected drug-related activity and the order aims to provide respite to residents and protect them from disruption Closure Orders can be obtained by councils and police where a property is linked to serious nuisance, disorder or criminal activity The order will remain in place for three months initially. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

Его стендап строится на живых наблюдениях, бытовых историях и неожиданных поворотах, которые превращают обычные ситуации в мощные комедийные моменты. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester City & PUMA break ground with ‘AI first’ Posted on August 28, 2026 by staff Manchester City & PUMA break ground with ‘AI first’ Club’s 2026/27 third kit marks first time in professional football that a fan has designed a kit using AI tools Share: SportTech Retail Manchester City & PUMA have announced an ‘AI first’ with the reveal of the club’s 2026/27 third kit. It marks the first time in professional football that a fan has designed a kit using AI tools. PUMA AI Creator is a custom generative AI tool that turns written prompts into kit designs within seconds – with no design experience required. Fans from over 200 countries brought forward their vision for what the third kit should look like, resulting in over 180,000 unique shirts. Following 1.7 million platform ratings, the most popular kits were shortlisted to the final 10, which went to fan vote in January 2025. With votes having been submitted by the club’s global fanbase, the winner was crowned: a white base split by a central two-tone sash, half sky blue, half navy, running the length of the shirt with a subtle gradient effect that shifts as it catches the light. Behind the winning kit was lifelong City fan Elliott. “City has been part of my life for as long as I can remember, so to have designed a kit that will now be worn by the players is a genuine honour,” he said. “I’ve always loved football shirts and design, and I created mine using PUMA AI Creator on my lunch break, never imagining it could actually become a City kit. “The whole experience has been incredible, from seeing people react to the design, to seeing it on the players for the first time when I was invited to the kit shoot. He has a catalogue of goals that would suggest that wasn't the worst idea, but Amorim's ulterior motives were also clear. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Events EU €3 Customs Duty Rule 2026: What This Means for UK Exporters EU €3 Customs Duty Rule 2026: What This Means for UK Exporters Official Chamber Post FREE Online Thursday 10 Sep 10am - 11am Book Now About the event The way low-value goods enter the European Union is changing From 1 July 2026, the EU introduced a new €3 customs duty on low-value consignments valued up to €150 entering the EU from outside the bloc. The change removes the previous duty exemption and introduces new considerations for businesses exporting goods directly to EU customers The new duty applies based on product categories/tariff classifications rather than simply per parcel, meaning shipments containing different types of goods could face multiple charges. For example, a parcel containing products under different tariff headings may attract multiple While the change is aimed largely at addressing the growth of low-value e-commerce imports, it will also impact UK businesses selling products directly into EU markets, including online retailers, brands and SMEs What the new €3 EU customs duty means for UK businesses
